Distribution. The only known specimen of Ch. baiocchii sp. nov. was collected in southern Iran, at an altitude of 2050 m, 7 km west of Dasht-e-Arzhan village, a locality situated in the upper Qara Agaj valley, in the southern offshoots of the Zagros mountain range (Figs 15, 16). The area is characterized by very dry, rocky ground, with sparse arboreal cover, predominantely formed by Quercus sp., together with Crataegus, Fraxinus, and other genera, with a sparse ground flora of herbaceous plants. Phenology. Chrysura baiocchii sp. nov. was found in May.
